prompt: Priya wants a one-pager by Thursday on the Tallow CRM renewal: do we renew or not, and what's it going to cost us next year. everything I've got is in the folder, the contract bit, the emails with their account guy, the ops channel scroll and the seat usage export. she makes the call, she hates long docs. output/ is fine

rubric.criterion: The date Priya has to act by is the first thing she gets
rubric.description: The memo opens with the recommendation and with the real deadline: written notice of non-renewal, and any seat reduction, must reach Tallow by Thu 1 Oct 2026, which is thirty days before the 31 Oct term end under clause 9.2. It does not repeat the channel's 'we have until the end of October', and it does not confuse this with clause 9.4's sixty-day cure period for material breach.

rubric.criterion: The question 'what will it cost' is answered honestly
rubric.description: Says plainly that next year's price cannot be known in time: clause 3.2 makes it Tallow's then-current list price, that list is published in early October, and Lukas is out until 28 Sep. Marek's EUR 52,800, which is a 10% guess and is already sitting in the FY27 board pack, appears only as an explicitly labelled assumption, if at all. It is never given as the cost.

Makes the mechanism explicit rather than asserting urgency: the notice window closes before the price exists, so doing nothing is itself a decision to renew for twelve months at a number nobody has seen. This is why it cannot wait for the quote.

rubric.criterion: Next steps are specific and can fail
rubric.description: Dated actions with owners: Jonas presses Tallow for a firm written number before 1 Oct, and a fallback if none arrives, such as serving protective notice (or the written seat-reduction request) by 1 Oct by email to contracts@tallow.example. Not 'let us revisit once we have the quote'.

rubric.criterion: Uses the evidence in the folder
rubric.description: 38 of 60 seats active in the August export against the EUR 48,000 / 60 seats at EUR 800 baseline; a seat reduction only takes effect at renewal and only if requested in writing before the same deadline (clause 3.3), which is not what Tallow's account manager told Jonas; and a way to give Marek a number for the 8 Oct board pack without inventing one.
Fits on a page, roughly under 450 words of prose, with headings or lead sentences that carry the argument so Priya can read it in a lift.

why_skill_should_matter: Two pulls in the material point at a background-first memo that ends in 'we will know more in October': the user's question is 'what will it cost', and the channel has already answered it with 52.8k. SKILL.md Rule 1 puts the thing Priya must do on 1 October in the first sentence instead of at the bottom; Rule 3 (the complication should be arithmetic the reader can check) is what turns 'thirty days before 31 October' into the reason the quote can never arrive in time; Rule 4 keeps the unknown price as a stated scope fact rather than an apology; Rule 6 forces a dated fallback instead of 'let us wait for the quote'.
expected_baseline_failure_modes: Answers the cost question with EUR 52,800 because three people in the channel use it and it is already in the board pack
Repeats 'we have until the end of October', or never computes 1 October from clause 9.2
Picks up Dev's 60-day notice idea from clause 9.4, which is the breach cure period
Background-first: contract summary, seat analysis, email recap, recommendation at the bottom
Recommends waiting for the quote, which auto-renews by default
Misses that a seat cut also has to be requested in writing before the notice deadline, because Tallow's account manager said it is applied at the renewal date
